title: mintFor() bypasses global pause check, allowing minting during emergency stop
description: NFTMinterV2.mintFor() does not check the global `paused` state, unlike _executeMint() which enforces `require(!paused)` at line 171. When the contract is paused via the pauser role (intended as a global emergency stop), authorized minters -- including the NFTMigrator contract -- can still mint NFTs by calling mintFor(). This creates a gap in the emergency stop mechanism: the owner/pauser cannot fully halt all minting activity. If a vulnerability is discovered and the contract is emergency-paused, new V2 NFTs can still be minted via migration or any other authorized minter path.
impact: The global pause mechanism is incomplete. During an emergency (e.g., a discovered vulnerability in a dispatcher or the NFT claim redemption system), authorized minters can continue minting NFTs that may be compromised or that inflate supply when all activity should be frozen. The pauser role specifically exists for emergency response, and having mintFor bypass it undermines this safety mechanism.
attack_path: A vulnerability is discovered in a dispatcher or claim redemption logic.
Owner/pauser calls pause() to emergency-halt all minting.
User calls NFTMigrator.migrate() which calls v2.mintFor(index, user).
mintFor() has no pause check -- NFTs are minted despite the global pause.
Newly minted NFTs may be compromised or create unintended supply inflation.
recommendation: Add `require(!paused, "Contract is paused");` as the first check in mintFor(), consistent with _executeMint().
